title: On the Optimality of Kinship Naming: an Information-theoretic Approach
abstract: arXiv:2511.19120v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The structure of naming systems in natural languages hinges on a trade-off between high informativeness and low complexity. Focusing on the domain of kinship naming, we analyze such trade-off while addressing simplifying assumptions of prior work, namely: (i) universal communicative need across languages, and (ii) optimal listeners. To that aim, we collect data from four different languages, and analyze how different communicative needs and variations in the listener model influence the informativeness--complexity trade-off. Adopting a referential game setup from emergent communication, we further show that trade-off optimality is not only theoretically achievable but also emerges empirically in learned communication systems.

translated_title: 论亲属称谓命名的最优性：一种信息论方法
translated_abstract: 自然语言中命名系统的结构取决于高信息量与低复杂性之间的权衡。本文聚焦于亲属称谓命名领域，在分析这种权衡的同时，克服了先前工作中的简化假设，即：(i) 跨语言普遍一致的交际需求，以及 (ii) 理想最优的听者模型。为此，我们收集了四种不同语言的数据，并分析不同的交际需求以及听者模型的变化如何影响信息量-复杂性的权衡。通过采用涌现通信研究中的指称博弈框架，我们进一步表明，这种权衡的最优性不仅在理论上可以实现，而且在学习到的通信系统中也能经验性地涌现。
tldr: 该研究采用信息论方法分析四种语言的亲属称谓系统，克服了以往关于普遍交际需求和理想听者的简化假设，证明亲属命名结构在信息量与复杂性之间达到了最优权衡，且这种最优性在学习到的通信系统中也能实际涌现。
en_tdlr: This study uses an information-theoretic approach to analyze kinship naming systems across four languages, overcoming simplifying assumptions about universal communicative needs and optimal listeners, and shows that kinship naming achieves an optimal trade-off between informativeness and complexity, which also emerges empirically in learned communication systems.
